items.title: A failure of base change is witnessed by an algebraically closed field over a normal affine base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma makes the failure of the base change property concrete: if the property holds in degree q - 1 but fails in degree q, then there is a cartesian diagram with an affine, integral, normal base with algebraically closed function field, a dominant map from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field, and a cyclic coefficient sheaf of order dividing n whose higher direct image in degree q does not vanish (statement lines 17295-17317). The proof is a complete chain of named reductions: it starts from the diagram and sheaf prepared by the companion lemma (proof lines 17325-17327), makes the base affine (proof lines 17328-17329), makes the field algebraically closed through the integral top lemma (proof lines 17330-17331), replaces the coefficients by a constant cyclic sheaf using the decomposition of modules over the cyclic group (proof lines 17332-17335), and replaces the base by its normalization in that field through the integral bottom lemma (proof lines 17336-17338). The non-formal content is the sequence of reductions, each attributed. The claim is H2: a structured reduction with every input named.
